Circuit and end view:

        conventional current I
   ┌──────→──────(((( steel bar ))))──────┐
   │                   A          B       │
   │                                      │
   └─────────────── + |‖| − ─────────────┘
                         battery

Viewed from end A, draw the current around the turns anticlockwise (↺). This makes A the north pole and B the south pole.
steps: Connect the solenoid in series with a battery and a switch, with the steel bar placed inside the solenoid.
Choose the current direction so that, when viewed from end A, the current in the turns is anticlockwise.
By the clock rule for a solenoid, the end from which the current appears anticlockwise is a north pole; therefore A becomes N and B becomes S.
items.finalAnswer: The steel bar is magnetised with A as the north pole and B as the south pole by passing current through the solenoid in the direction shown.

items.figure:
One valid labeling (the labels may both be reversed):

       S  [ magnet 1 ]  N   gap   N  [ magnet 2 ]  S
                           ↑
                      compass N
                           │
                      compass S
                           ↑ north-south direction

Draw field lines emerging from both facing N poles and curving outward around the gap to enter the outer S poles. Do not draw field lines joining the two facing poles.
steps: Label the two poles facing each other alike. For example, label both facing poles N; then the outer ends are S. (The alternative, with both facing poles S and both outer ends N, is also correct.)
Draw magnetic field lines emerging from each N pole and entering an S pole. The lines curve away from the gap between the like poles and do not join across the gap.
At the midpoint, the magnetic fields due to the two identical magnets are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so their resultant field is zero.
With no resultant field from the magnets at the midpoint, the compass needle settles along the north-south direction.
items.finalAnswer: The facing poles are alike; either N–N or S–S is correct, with the compass at the midpoint pointing north-south because the magnetic fields there cancel.

The arrows show the magnetic field at O due to each solenoid, directed radially outward toward that solenoid. Mark clockwise current when looking from O at the inward-facing end of each coil.
steps: Draw the four identical solenoids symmetrically around O, with the same current magnitude in each.
Make the end of every solenoid facing O a south pole and its far end a north pole. Using the right-hand grip rule, show the current clockwise when viewed from O at each inward-facing end.
The magnetic field at O due to each solenoid is directed away from O, toward that solenoid. The four equal field vectors cancel when all four solenoids are on.

When any one solenoid is switched off, the other three fields have a resultant equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the field that was switched off. The resultant is therefore directed from O toward the switched-off solenoid.
items.finalAnswer: Show equal clockwise currents as viewed from O, so each inward-facing end is S and switching off any one solenoid leaves a resultant field directed toward it.

steps: The strength of a magnetic field is described by the closeness of its magnetic lines of force.
Where the lines of force are close together, the magnetic field is strong.
Where the lines of force are far apart, the magnetic field is weak.
For a uniform magnetic field, draw straight, parallel, equally spaced lines of force.
For a non-uniform magnetic field, draw lines that are not equally spaced; closer lines show the stronger region and farther-apart lines show the weaker region.
items.finalAnswer: A magnetic field is stronger where its lines of force are closer together and weaker where they are farther apart.

Circuit-breaker diagram:

 Live wire ────o/ o──────── Load ──── Neutral wire
                ↑
          movable contact
                │ iron armature
           [electromagnet]
                │
          current-carrying coil

Draw the movable contact so it normally touches the fixed contact. Show an overload current energising the electromagnet, which attracts the iron armature and opens the contact.
steps: A circuit breaker is a safety device that automatically breaks a circuit when the current exceeds the safe limit.
The current in the circuit passes through a coil in the circuit breaker, making the coil an electromagnet.
If an excessive current flows, the electromagnet becomes strong and attracts the iron armature.
The armature moves and separates the contacts, opening the circuit and stopping the current.
After the fault is removed, the circuit breaker can be reset.
items.finalAnswer: A circuit breaker automatically opens a circuit when excessive current makes its electromagnet attract an armature and separate the contacts.
